findings.where: Caption under the board, every screen (p.caption)
findings.what: The caption "Every speed is worked from the teeth through each mesh: speed × teeth is the same on both gears" shows from screen 1, so it gives away screen 7's rule before Dan finds it and prints the rule under typed puzzles 8, 10, 11 and 12, which the brief says he recalls; remove it, since the lead already says every count and speed is an example.

The brief promised the lesson opens on the five-gear puzzle with a prediction before anything moves, then three more chains to trace before the rule, but the build opens with screen 1 explaining and turning the gears, and screen 3 states the odd and even rule after only one traced chain; make screen 1 ask first ("The driver turns clockwise. Which way will the 20-tooth gear turn?") and move Mixed sizes and one more chain, such as a bent chain of six, ahead of Odd and even.

findings.where: Typed screens 8, 10, 11 and 12, the Why? button
findings.what: Why? works before any Check, so one tap prints the working and the figure (for example "720 ÷ 36 = 20 rev/min") before Dan has typed anything; hide Why? on typed steps until the first Check, as TYPED.md does by showing the working after two wrong tries.

findings.where: interactive.whatAmILookingAt (shown in the dossier as "What you're looking at")
findings.what: It describes a grid of pegs, gears waiting in a tray to drag onto pegs and a dropped gear closing a loop, but the build has none of these, because each screen sets out its own gears and only the driver turns, so rewrite it to match the built screens or build the drag-to-peg board the brief promised.

The cause, that the teeth of both gears move the same way at the mesh, is only in the words; the direction arcs sit on the tops of the gears, where the motion looks opposite, so add a small ink arrow at the mesh showing both teeth moving down together, as the triangle's red mesh already does for the conflict.

The step from "the teeth at the mesh move the same way" to "the gears turn opposite ways" is skipped on screen, so add the explanation's own line: the driver's right-hand teeth move down, they push the next gear's left-hand teeth down, and that is anticlockwise.

The screen gives n₁T₁ = n₂T₂ without saying what n and T are, and it skips the step that a gear passes its own tooth count every turn, so teeth a minute = speed × teeth; add that sentence and "n is the speed in rev/min and T the number of teeth" (it stays under 70 words).
"The same 720 teeth a minute" relies on screen 8's Why?, which Dan may never have opened if he worked by the ratio, so write "60 × 12 = 720 teeth a minute pass each mesh".

Before the idler fades in, the 36-tooth gear already shows "20 rev/min" and a driver's-way arrow while it touches nothing, so fade its arrow and speed in with the idler, or flip its arrow as the idler arrives, so the change visibly comes from the idler.

findings.where: Screen 5 (Close the loop), the locked triangle
findings.what: The locked triangle has no grab, so trying to turn it gives no response at all; let its driver be grabbed, with the red mesh pulsing or the gears rocking a hair, so Dan feels the lock rather than finding a dead picture.

A single 18 : 72 pair puts a winch drum at 360 rev/min, far faster than a real winch, whose boxes run from about 21 : 1 upwards in lesson 2's own figures, so call it a plain drum drive or add one sentence that a real winch adds more stages, as lesson 2 shows.

findings.where: Screen 13, hint on "It turns, but slower"
findings.what: "Sizes change the speed in a line" does not fit five equal 12-tooth gears, so say instead that a gear of the same size cannot slow the ring, and ask him to count the gears in it now.

"The ampere-turn balance also says nothing about direction" sits badly with an electrician who knows that the secondary's ampere-turns oppose the primary's, which is why they balance, so give a true break instead: a transformer's polarity depends on how its windings are wound and connected, while every outside mesh always reverses.

findings.where: Screen 2 picture (five in a line, 360 light and dark moved)
findings.what: The ordinals 1st to 5th hang from each gear's rim, so they sit at three different heights; put them on one baseline under the row.

findings.where: Pick screens 2, 4, 6 and 13, the chosen answer
findings.what: A chosen answer is filled ink exactly like the Check button below it, in light and dark, so two identical filled buttons sit together; mark the chosen answer with an ink outline or a tick instead.
The three answers sit in one row and "It turns, but slower" wraps to two lines, so its button is taller than the other two; give the row's buttons one height.

findings.where: Lesson as a whole, against the brief
findings.what: The brief promised one screen on an internal gear keeping the direction, but the build mentions it only in "ignores"; add it as a short SHOW or say in the brief that it moved.
Footnotes [^1] and [^3] are repeated in the summary line after appearing in the body, so drop the repeats and keep the lesson to three markers.
